title: Seoul's Incheon Named Busiest International Airport
paragraphs: Incheon International Airport, near Seoul, has become the busiest airport in the world for international passengers, according to new data.

The data came from Airports Council International, or ACI, a group that represents airports around the world. In the first six months of 2026, Incheon had 38.39 million international passengers. This was more than London's Heathrow Airport, which had 37.79 million and was second. Singapore's Changi Airport was third, with 34.53 million. It is the first time that Incheon has been first in this ranking. However, the numbers are not final yet.

Why did Incheon do so well? According to the company that runs the airport, one reason is problems with travel in the Middle East because of the war between the US and Iran. Because of this, some travelers have stopped flying through airports such as Dubai and started traveling through East Asia instead. In fact, the number of people changing planes at Incheon rose 18.1% to 4.24 million in the first half of the year. Dubai was second in the ranking in 2024 and 2025, but it may not even be in the top five this year.

Incheon Airport opened in 2001, and it is about 48 kilometers from Seoul. Today, 101 airlines fly from there to 183 cities. It was 10th in the ranking in 2002, fifth in 2018 and third in 2024 and 2025. In 2024, the airport was made bigger, and now it can handle 106 million passengers a year.
Meanwhile, in Europe, Istanbul Airport in Turkey has become busier than Heathrow when all passengers are counted.

However, this ranking only counts international passengers. If domestic passengers are also counted, the busiest airport in the world is still Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport in the United States.
